title: Redwood discovery - Helix Robotics latency & throughput
summary: Discovery focused on Helix's production targets: p95 end-to-end latency for streaming chat <= 300ms for short responses, concurrency target ~75 sustained, aggregate tokens/sec target ~3k-5k. Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, VPC/private deployment questions, and a benchmark pilot. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share pricing, run a short benchmark using Helix sample prompts, provide SOC2/KMS docs, and schedule a dedicated benchmarking slot w/Helix infra team.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Hayes: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, we're Jordan with Redwood, and with me is Priya and Liam. Quick intro?
[00:07] Evan Park: Hey Jordan, Evan here, CTO at Helix Robotics. Marta, Samir and Rina are on.
[00:10] Marta Lopez: Hi all. We're looking at how to serve our medium-context agent responses with good latency under load.
[00:18] Jordan Hayes: Great, high-level today is latency and throughput p95 targets, concurrency, streaming behavior, does that sound right?
[00:22] Evan Park: Yes, exactly. Our use case: on-device controller + cloud talk. The cloud runs higher-level planning for edge robots; typical responses are 20-120 tokens; occasional long policy dumps ~800 tokens.
[00:35] Priya Malhotra: Thanks. A couple clarifying Qs: what's your p95 SLO target for the short responses, and what's your expected peak concurrent requests?
[00:41] Marta Lopez: For short responses we want p95 <= 300ms if possible - end-to-end streaming start-to-first-token ideally under 200-250ms. Concurrency: sustained ~60-80 concurrent sessions, spiky to 150 during fleet rollouts.
[00:54] Samir Patel: Important: some customers use streaming in real-time dashboards so token-level latency matters. We care about token/sec throughput overall: target aggregate ~3k tokens/sec but with bursts to 8k.
[01:05] Liam Chen: Good, that helps. Are you evaluating hosted, dedicated or private deployments?
[01:09] Evan Park: All three. Pilot on hosted to move fast; if numbers or data residency require, then dedicated or private.
[01:16] Rina Okafor: For private, we need KMS integration and SSO/SAML; SOC2 and audit logs are must-haves.
[01:22] Jordan Hayes: Totally. Quick call-out: Hosted gets you fastest time-to-value; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you control for KMS and networking. We'll share our SOC2 artifact and KMS integration notes.
[01:33] Marta Lopez: Can you share concrete numbers? What p95 have you hit for streaming chat on hosted?
[01:38] Priya Malhotra: Sure. On our Redwood-hosted endpoints, we've seen p95 first-token latencies around 180-280ms for 64-token responses on optimized models and geos close to region. For dedicated with pinned capacity we can get more consistent sub-200ms p95 at similar model sizes. But depends on model, quantization, and request concurrency.
[01:58] Evan Park: When you say model sizes - are we talking 7B, 13B, or larger? Because our workload is currently on a fine-tuned 13B.
[02:05] Priya Malhotra: 13B is a common sweet spot. For a 13B with q4/8 or bfloat quant profile on modern GPUs, p95 for first token can be ~200ms at moderate concurrency. The per-token generation latency for streaming is ~20-40ms/token depending on chunking and batch size.
[02:20] Samir Patel: And aggregate tokens/sec - how do you scale that? Is that autoscaling or dedicated lanes?
[02:25] Liam Chen: Two knobs: dedicated reserved capacity gives you a fixed number of concurrent model workers; autoscaling can add workers but has scale-up latency. We also do prefix/KV cache and batching; caching helps reduce work for repeated prompts. For tokens/sec you can think of per-GPU sustained throughput - e.g., a single GPU can do X tokens/sec for your model variant; we'll provide benchmark numbers in the pilot.
[02:47] Marta Lopez: We need numbers for our 13B fine-tuned: target is sustain 3k tokens/sec with p95 <= 300ms. Is that feasible on hosted?
[02:55] Priya Malhotra: Feasible at scale, but hosted shared pools can be subject to noisy neighbors; we can often meet the target in most regions but for strict SLOs we'd recommend Dedicated or Private where you get reserved capacity and predictable latency.
[03:06] Evan Park: For Dedicated - what's the typical sizing? How many GPUs for 75 concurrency and 3k tokens/sec?
[03:12] Liam Chen: Ballpark: depends on sequence lengths and batching. For 13B, if average response is 64 tokens and generate speed ~30 tokens/sec per GPU, you'd need about 3-4 GPUs to hit 3k tokens/sec assuming efficient batching and continuous streaming; to handle spikes and concurrency headroom we'd suggest a pool of 6-8 GPUs with autoscale and burst capacity. We'll validate in benchmark.
[03:33] Samir Patel: Can you also test cold-starts? We care about KV cache priming and first-request latencies when model weights are swapped.
[03:39] Priya Malhotra: Yes, our benchmark harness includes cold vs warm scenarios, priming caches, and multi-tenant stress tests. We'll run both hosted-equivalent and dedicated pool tests.
[03:49] Rina Okafor: For private, we need to know about networking: can the control plane sit in our VPC? How do you handle data plane traffic?
[03:56] Jordan Hayes: For Redwood Private we provide a customer-managed networking model: control plane can be private or hosted, and data plane runs in your VPC. We support customer KMS/HSM for key management and provide audit logs. We'll share docs.
[04:06] Evan Park: Any limitations on streaming vs non-streaming in private?
[04:09] Priya Malhotra: No limitations - streaming works the same. The main differences are orchestration and observability integrations are run in your network; latency is then primarily your infra and placement.
[04:18] Marta Lopez: Can you walk through a sample benchmark plan?
[04:21] Liam Chen: Sure - step A: Redwood runs an initial synthetic benchmark with your sample prompt set in our hosted env to baseline latency and throughput. Step B: run dedicated pool benchmark with pinned GPUs that simulate your concurrency/peak patterns. Step C (if private): run on your network or a lab with your infra to validate network+resource constraints. We'll provide a benchmark report with p50/p95/p99, token/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, error rates, and suggestions for batching and quantization.
[04:46] Evan Park: Timeline? We want to start a pilot next week if possible.
[04:50] Jordan Hayes: We can spin up a hosted benchmark within 3-5 business days with your prompt set and a small auth key. Dedicated pilot depends on contract and capacity but can start in 1-2 weeks. Private depends on onboarding and network setup - typically 2-4 weeks.
[05:03] Rina Okafor: Please send SOC2 and the KMS integration doc; also who will own the penetration test coordination?
[05:09] Jordan Hayes: We'll send SOC2, KMS integration notes, and security contact info. Redwood security will coordinate pen test scheduling; we'll include the contact in the docs.
[05:18] Marta Lopez: One more question - do you support multi-region failover for Dedicated? We need our agents to remain available if a region has issues.
[05:25] Priya Malhotra: Yes, policy-based routing can route between pools; we also have automatic fallback to compatible model variants if primary capacity is constrained. There is a tradeoff: cross-region adds RTT but improves availability.
[05:36] Samir Patel: On pricing - do you charge per-token for hosted and monthly for dedicated? Is there a blended model with reserved commit + overage?
[05:44] Jordan Hayes: Hosted is usage-based per token and per embedding unit. Dedicated is reserved capacity contracts (monthly/annual) with a base commitment and overage pricing. We'll include a sample SOW and pricing sheet in the follow-up.
[05:54] Evan Park: Ok good. Quick recap and next steps?
[05:57] Jordan Hayes: Recap: Redwood to run hosted benchmark with Helix prompts, share SOC2/KMS docs, provide dedicated sizing recommendations and sample pricing, and schedule a dedicated benchmarking slot with Samir and Marta next week.
[06:08] Marta Lopez: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[06:10] Jordan Hayes: Thanks - we'll follow up via email with links and proposed times.
[06:12] [end of recording]
